commenti.body: That clip sounds like it was a smaller section of Thomas Flights video In Praise Of Bad Continuity. It doesn’t go in depth into Schoonmakers editing style but generally discusses why there are frequent continuity errors throughout their collaborative works. Thomas Flight should a number of other video essays on editing, and I know at least one video that looked at The Killers Of The Flower Moon and some of the editing choices made within that film.
(Sorry I wrote this comment with so much filler as though it’s an essay, but I was trying to get through the word limit filter)
It’s basically about using the best take—meaning the most well-performed—which invokes the most emotion in the viewer if the script is lively and well-written. At least that’s how I understood it.
